fields.description:
## Mode Precondition

This epic applies only when enforcement.strategy=ci AND merge.strategy=pr AND a remote is present (verified by git remote get-url origin). At sprint Phase A, the orchestrator detects mode and emits exactly one of two banners: "MODE: ci-pr" (epic mechanisms active) or "MODE: local — per-story PR mechanisms inactive" (existing local workflow unchanged, no breakage). Local-mode parity is filed as a follow-on epic with this scope: TrackerDefenseStore per-story SHA-range support, in-session /dso:review story-close trigger, local Strategy E equivalent, shared pre-merge validation, dual-mode trailer linking.

## Glossary

- session worktree: Claude Code working directory for a sprint
- session branch: git branch checked out there, source of the long-lived draft PR
- story branch: story/<ticket-id> forked from session branch at story dispatch
- Phase A/E/F/I: sprint orchestration phases (Init / Task Dispatch / Post-Batch Processing / Primary Ticket Closure)
- Strategy A: per-story PR + size-gate (this epic)
- Strategy E: region-split FALLBACK for oversized review surfaces
- hash-of-record: diff_hash + SHA range recorded with each attestation, defining the exact range covered
- long-lived draft PR: single draft PR (session→main) opened at Phase A and refreshed across all stories
- claim-fingerprint: SHA-256 of lowercased, whitespace-normalized claim text
- SPRINT_SESSION_ID: sprint-init-generated UUID; written to .sprint-active marker file at Phase A and exposed to CI as a repository variable (vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID) refreshed by a Phase A step
- sprint-active state: presence of .sprint-active marker file in artifacts dir; created Phase A, removed Phase I

## Context

Today's review pipeline becomes unreliable on large PRs. Empirical PR data on this project since 2026-04-27 (~50 merged) shows every >2-cycle PR was ≥500 LOC and ≥10 files; PR #37 at ~4000 LOC escalated to user with "findings have not converged." Published research (SmartBear/Cisco, Microsoft Research, Google eng-practices) converges on ~200–400 LOC as the reliability cliff. Review-pipeline-side hardening (closed epic 6da2-4cff) addressed reviewer calibration but not surface area. The lever is splitting review into per-story increments on a single long-lived draft PR (Strategy A), with attestation accumulating across stories so the final epic→main merge re-reviews only the unattested delta.

The current /dso:sprint workflow harvests per-task worktrees back to a shared session worktree without per-story isolation, batches mix tasks from multiple stories, and observed reality is that some sub-agents write directly to the session worktree despite worktree.isolation_enabled=true — no leakage detector exists today. This epic adds story-isolated branches with deterministic trailer-based attribution (composing on top of hard dependency 170b-2ac9, which delivers the git-trailer injection library, the DSO-Story/DSO-Task/DSO-Epic trailer schema, and the attribution.enabled config gate), restricts session-worktree commits to merges, fires CI llm-review per-story push against a draft PR pre-created at sprint init, and routes oversized story deltas through a true region-split FALLBACK path (Strategy E) — the current FALLBACK passes the whole diff to one reviewer.

## Success Criteria

1. Mode detection and ci-pr gating: At Phase A, sprint orchestrator detects mode and emits a banner. Local-mode users see "MODE: local — per-story PR mechanisms inactive" and proceed with existing workflow unchanged. ci-pr-mode users see "MODE: ci-pr" and continue with Phase A draft PR creation. Verification: integration test with mocked git remote get-url returning empty asserts banner is "MODE: local" and no gh pr create invocation occurs; with remote present + ci-pr config asserts "MODE: ci-pr" and PR creation proceeds.

2. Story-isolated branches with merge gating (ci-pr mode only): Sprint creates story/<id> per dispatched story; merges into session branch only after that story's CI llm-review attests passed; orphan trailer commits route to story/orphan-<sprint-session-id>. Verification: post-sprint validation script asserts (a) git branch --list story/* shows exactly one branch per dispatched story plus optionally the orphan branch; (b) git log --merges <session-branch> shows one merge commit per story containing a DSO-Story trailer matching the story ID; (c) no non-merge commit appears on the session branch between story merges.

3. Mandatory DSO-Story trailer with explicit --message injection (ci-pr mode only): Sprint-mode commits via /dso:commit carry a DSO-Story (or routed orphan) trailer; session-branch merges constructed by the orchestrator using git merge --no-ff --message=<msg-with-trailer> so trailers survive on every merge SHA. Pre-commit hook validates trailer presence and rejects commits without a DSO trailer. Verification: (a) trailer-less commit rejected with documented error; (b) integration test asserts git interpret-trailers --parse <merge-sha> returns the DSO-Story line on every story-merge SHA; (c) test outside sprint mode with attribution.enabled=false asserts no enforcement.

4. Session-worktree merge-only policy and deterministic leakage handling (ci-pr mode only): Pre-commit hook scoped to sprint-active state via .sprint-active marker file (created Phase A, removed Phase I). Hook accepts merge commits and rejects all non-merge commits with a clear error directing the user to a story worktree. Escape hatch: setting DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0 env var bypasses the hook for emergency commits with an audit log entry. The release pipeline (merge-to-main.sh) operates outside sprint-active state so its non-merge commits are accepted. When a non-merge commit lands on the session branch (bypassing the hook), the post-Phase-F leakage detector cherry-picks it onto the branch named by its DSO-Story trailer; orphan trailers route to story/orphan-<sprint-session-id>; missing-trailer commits cause sprint to hard-fail with a manual-attribution prompt; closed-story-trailer commits hard-fail with named recovery options (rebase-and-retag with git rebase -i and manual trailer edit, or --force-route-to=<story-id> override flag); cherry-pick conflicts trigger git cherry-pick --abort and emit a hard-fail with the conflicting commit SHA and named conflicting paths. Verification: 5 test cases covering each path including the closed-story-recovery flag exercise.

5. Long-lived draft PR with per-story CI review and region-split FALLBACK (ci-pr mode only): At Phase A the orchestrator opens a draft PR via gh pr create --draft, completing before any story-branch dispatch in Phase E (PR creation is a Phase A blocking step, not concurrent with Phase E push triggers). The merge-to-main-pr.sh "refuse if open PR exists" guard is amended to "refuse if non-draft PR exists" — draft PRs are expected for the long-lived pattern. A new workflow file fires CI llm-review on every push to story/* branches, scoped to merge-base(session, story/<branch>)..story/<branch>, with concurrency-group keyed ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID }} (using vars context per GitHub Actions docs — env is not allowed in concurrency expressions). The PR-scoped GitHubPRDefenseStore is active from day one. When a story-branch delta exceeds 400 LOC or 15 files, the HUGE-diff FALLBACK path activates true region-split review: file-clustered regions reviewed in parallel by tier-appropriate reviewers, findings deduplicated on (file, line-range, dimension, claim-fingerprint) with line-range overlap matching (not exact-match), conflicting severities resolved to MAX, both rationales preserved as a merged-rationale field when severities differ (no silent rationale discard), opus arch synthesis pass for boundary-only issues. Verification: 5 test cases including overlapping-region fixture asserting dedup with MAX-severity and dual-rationale preservation, and second-push assertion that DefenseStore returns prior attestations on the same story branch.

6. Hash-of-record protocol (ci-pr mode only): Each attestation records the diff_hash at the time of attestation plus the SHA range it covers (story-branch tip SHA, story-branch base SHA). DefenseStore.load_for_region validates by SHA-range membership, not by diff_hash equality alone. Merge commits do not invalidate attestations whose covered SHA range is preserved in the merge ancestry. Verification: integration test merges story A into the session branch, then queries DefenseStore for story A's attestations from a final-PR-context session and asserts the attestations are returned (not stale-invalidated).

7. Bug 4724-41a7 fix as Phase 1 prerequisite (applies to all modes): Resolution of bug 4724-41a7 (Claude Code creates sub-agent worktrees from main repo HEAD instead of session HEAD when orchestrator is in a session worktree) ships as Phase 1 of this epic, before any story-branch infrastructure depends on it. Regression test: dispatching a sub-agent from a session worktree with worktree.isolation_enabled=true produces a sub-agent worktree whose base SHA equals the session HEAD SHA, not the main HEAD SHA. Verification: regression test runs at every CI invocation thereafter.

8. Validation acceptance with inline value-signal (ci-pr mode only): A validation sprint of at least 1500 total changed LOC across at least 3 stories runs the entire pipeline end-to-end and lands one final PR to main. Mechanical proxies: (a) the long-lived draft PR exists from Phase A; (b) every story merge into the session branch carries a DSO-Story trailer readable by git interpret-trailers; (c) each story-branch CI run produces a reviewer-findings.json and writes to GitHubPRDefenseStore; (d) on the final PR ready-for-review transition, DefenseStore.load_for_region returns attestations covering each merged story branch; (e) the leakage detector test suite passes 5-case matrix. Inline value-signal assertion: re-reviewed-LOC / total-LOC < 50% (loose falsifiable threshold to confirm the mechanism reduces re-review surface). The headline "<15% LOC re-reviewed" target is filed as a follow-on observability ticket with continuous tracking via the sprint summary log.

## Scenario Analysis

Surviving high-confidence scenarios from Red Team + Blue Team filter, each addressed by an SC or risk mitigation:

- Cherry-pick conflicts on shared-file leaked commits (critical, runtime) — addressed by SC4 hard-fail with abort + named conflict paths.
- Hash-rewriting cascade across task→story→session merges (critical, runtime) — addressed by SC6 hash-of-record protocol with SHA-range membership lookup.
- DSO-Story trailer points to deleted/closed story (high, runtime) — addressed by SC4 named-recovery options (rebase-and-retag or --force-route-to override).
- Region-split cross-boundary findings rationale loss (high, runtime) — addressed by SC5 dual-rationale preservation.
- Pre-commit hook rejects merge-to-main-pr.sh's own non-merge commits (high, runtime) — addressed by SC4 sprint-active-scoped hook + non-sprint-mode release pipeline.
- CI rate-limit exhaustion under parallel story-push storm (high, runtime) — addressed by SC5 concurrency-group keying via vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID.
- attribution.enabled=false bypass route (high, configuration) — addressed by SC3 sprint-mode override of project config.
- merge-to-main-pr.sh refuse-if-open-PR guard conflicts with single-long-lived-draft-PR pattern (high, deployment) — addressed by SC5 guard amendment to non-draft-only.
- DefenseStore PR-keyed empty for non-PR refs (critical, runtime) — addressed by SC5 pre-create draft PR at Phase A so PR-scoped store is active from day one.
- Bug 4724-41a7 cascade if unresolved (critical, deployment) — addressed by SC7 phasing as Phase 1 prerequisite.
- Phase A PR-creation race vs first push (medium, runtime) — addressed by SC5 explicit ordering: PR creation blocks Phase E dispatch.
- Sprint-active escape hatch ambiguity (medium, configuration) — addressed by SC4 .sprint-active marker file + DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0 env override with audit logging.
- Story-branch cleanup race vs in-flight CI (medium, runtime) — addressed by branch retention until Phase I (no mid-sprint cleanup).
- Orphan-trailer branch unbounded growth (medium, deployment) — bounded by sprint-session scope; ephemeral, cleared at Phase I; documented as known limitation.

## Dependencies

- Hard: 170b-2ac9 (Commit-level source attribution via git-native trailers) must reach closed before this epic enters sprint. Provides DSO-Task/DSO-Story/DSO-Epic trailer infrastructure and attribution.enabled config gate.
- Hard: dbbc-cf67-8cfc-4b4d (Stateful re-review with arbitration) ships DefenseStore.load_for_region() with the no-op default; this epic depends on the interface and activates real region loading.
- Closed prerequisite: 6da2-4cff-ff38-4056 (review-reliability hardening).
- Subsumes: 1083-fb3d (PR-based merge) — this epic absorbs PR-creation scope including the long-lived draft PR pattern. Phase 0 step: ticket list-descendants 1083-fb3d; close as superseded or re-parent each child under this epic before sprint kickoff.
- Disambiguation gate (Phase 0): e407-d35c (possible duplicate of 170b-2ac9) — must be closed-as-duplicate or scoped-as-distinct before sprint kickoff.
- Boundary cross-references:
  - vs 70f6-05f1 (worktree isolation parallel review): this epic owns story-branch naming and merge-only restriction; that epic owns clash detection.
  - vs 6d90-93d5 (Conventional Commits enforcement): this epic owns post-commit CI region-split dedup; that epic owns pre-commit Conventional Commits format.
  - vs 7575-5a90 (static-analysis defense): independent attestation lookups; no shared store mutation.
  - vs 4911-c7ba (reviewer rubric expansion): reviewer agent interface must reach stable contract before Phase 4 wires the per-story CI review.

## Approach

One-shot delivery with phased internal ordering enforced via inter-story dependency declarations during preplanning:

- Phase 0 (sprint init): resolve 1083-fb3d descendants and e407-d35c disambiguation gate.
- Phase 1: bug 4724-41a7 fix (foundation; all later phases depend on it).
- Phase 2: trailer enforcement + sprint-active marker + session-worktree merge-only hook + Phase A mode-detection banner.
- Phase 3: story branches + leakage cherry-pick + long-lived draft PR (subsumes 1083-fb3d's PR-creation work).
- Phase 4: CI workflow on story/* push (using vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID) + DefenseStore region activation + Strategy E region-split FALLBACK with file-clustering, parallel reviewers, line-range-overlap dedup, MAX-severity reconciliation with dual-rationale preservation, and opus arch synthesis pass.
- Phase 5: hash-of-record protocol with SHA-range membership attestation lookup.

## Risk Mitigations

- R1 trailer injection (SC3 explicit --message construction)
- R2 PR-keyed defense (SC5 pre-create draft PR at Phase A)
- R3 hash cascade (SC6 hash-of-record + SHA-range lookup)
- R4 cherry-pick conflicts (SC4 abort + named conflict paths)
- R5 PR guard conflict (SC5 amendment to non-draft-only)
- R6 4724-41a7 cascade (SC7 phasing as Phase 1)
- R7 CI concurrency context (SC5 vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID, not env)
- R8 mode scoping (SC1 banner + ci-pr precondition)
- R9 deleted-story recovery (SC4 named recovery options)
- R10 cross-boundary rationale loss (SC5 dual-rationale preservation)

### Planning Intelligence Log

- Web research (Step 2.6): triggered. Bright-line conditions fired: External integration (GitHub Actions trigger semantics, gh CLI draft-PR creation, git interpret-trailers behavior on merge commits, GitHub stacked-PR community patterns); Novel architectural pattern (incremental review attestation across long-lived branch). Key findings: SmartBear/Cisco 200-400 LOC reliability cliff; Kubernetes/Gatsby/Mozilla single-PR incremental review patterns; GitLab MR 77758 trailer-on-merge fragility; GitHub Actions concurrency env-context restriction.
- Scenario analysis (Step 2.75): triggered (≥5 SCs + integration signals — full mode). 14 surviving scenarios after Blue Team filter, all addressed by SCs or documented as known limitations.
- Practitioner-requested additional cycles: 1 — local-enforcement / direct-merge / no-remote red team → spec scoped to ci-pr mode only with follow-on epic for local-mode parity.
- Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0): not triggered (epic is the originating brainstorm; prior follow-ons resolved).
- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): triggered (4 specialist re-review cycles); critical capability gap on git-interpret-trailers-on-merge resolved via SC3 explicit --message construction; integration_risk on env-context concurrency resolved via SC5 vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID.
- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): triggered — keywords: skill file modifications (sprint SKILL.md), hook behavioral logic (pre-commit hooks). Bot-psychologist deferred to implementation-plan stage where actual prompt drafts exist.
- Scale context (Step 0): empirical (~5 PRs/week, 20-25% currently exceed 400 LOC threshold); not inferred. Strategy E region-split activation threshold pinned at 400 LOC / 15 files per SmartBear research.
